scope: J293/T8103 built-in keyboard transport: PMGR power, pinmux/GPIO, Apple SPI controller PIO, Apple SPI-HID protocol, m1n1 HV interaction, and the Darwin HID-to-console path. Read-only. No hardware, SSH, build, boot or goal API. ADT facts are topology only; no serial/ECID/identity values are recorded.

inputs.reference: sources/linux-aurora-keyboard-reference (omacom/linux-aurora 6a08a08e). All 6 files rehashed: sha256 and git blob equal reports/sprint-010/native-keyboard-source-acquisition.json.
inputs.native_adt: private runs/m1-display-010/attempt-002/guest/original-adt.bin, parsed by a scratch reader (not copied into the repo).
inputs.secondary_dt_reference: An Asahi-derived t8103.dtsi/t8103-j293.dts outside this lab; used only to cross-check, superseded by root's private Linux FDT capture (SPI clock 120 MHz, spien AP GPIO 195, IRQ NUB GPIO 13, CS 65 us, 8 MHz).

verdict: No contradiction between the native ADT, root's Linux FDT capture and the pinned reference. A native transport is feasible under the current HV without HV changes. Do not port five reference defects listed below. A transport that works is not yet a shell keyboard: the HID event path must also deliver keyboard-page usages to PDHIDPushKeyboardEvent.

controller.adt: /arm-io/spi3 compatible 'spi-1,spimc', reg 0x23510c000 size 0x4000, AIC interrupt 0x269 (617), clock-gates 0x34, clock-ids 0x17b, dma-channels via sio-dma
controller.linux: apple,t8103-spi at 0x23510c000, AIC 617, clk 120 MHz, power-domain ps_spi3, pins AP 46-49 function 1

device.adt: /arm-io/spi3/ipd compatible 'hid-transport,spi'; interrupt-parent nub-gpio; interrupts <13 0x06000001>; reg words <0 0x7d 0x08010000 0 0x4e20 ...>; function-spi_en <AP gpio 195 0x00010101>; function-enable_cs <AP gpio 49 0x101>; spi3 function-spi_cs0 <AP gpio 49 1>; reset-sequence names function-spi_en
device.linux: apple,spi-hid-transport cs 0, 8 MHz, cs setup/hold 65 us, cs inactive 250 us, spien AP 195, IRQ NUB 13 level-low
decoding_inferences: 0x4e20 = 20000 ns = Apple's 20 us CS delay; Linux's 65 us is 20 + 45 us.

Top byte 0x06 of the interrupt flags probably selects GPIO interrupt group 6. nub-gpio lists supported-int-groups 4,5,6. Linux instead forces group 0 (pinctrl-apple-gpio.c:316-317) and works. Unverified.

power.hv_interaction: m1n1 map_essential hooks the PMGR registers of UART0, ATCn_USB and ATCn_USB_AON and their parents (hv/__init__.py:1473-1514). That chain includes SIO and SIO_BUSIF but not SPI3 or SPI_P. Guest writes to SIO/SIO_BUSIF are forced to target 0xf and later reads are shadowed (actual = target). Guest writes to SPI3 reach hardware.
power.procedure: Per pmgr-pwrstate.c:62-130: read the PS word; clear DEV_DISABLE(10), PS_RESET(12), AUTO_ENABLE(28), the write-1-to-clear WAS_CLKGATED/WAS_PWRGATED (8,9), BUSY(11) and TARGET(3:0); set TARGET=0xf; write; poll ACTUAL(7:4)==0xf, 1 us steps, 100 us budget. AUTO_ENABLE is optional; omit it for first bring-up.
safety: Never touch SPI3 MMIO until SPI3 ACTUAL reads 0xf. Accessing a gated block can take an SError or hang.
Record bit 31 (RESET) and do not change it. Linux has no reset for spi3 and works, so it is expected clear (inference).
SPI3 is not default-on in the ADT, so a native driver that skips the power step should be expected to fail, not to work by luck.

pins_and_gpio.register_layout: pinctrl-apple-gpio.c:46-68. Pin word at base + 4*pin: DATA bit0, MODE 3:1 (1 out, 3 IRQ low, 7 input/IRQ off), PERIPH 6:5, INPUT_ENABLE 9, GRP 18:16, LOCK 21. IRQ status at base + 0x800 + 0x40*group + 4*(pin/32).
pins_and_gpio.spi_pins: AP pins 46-49 (0x23c1000b8..0x23c1000c4) must be PERIPH=1 so the controller's CS bit drives pin 49 (CS) along with SCK/MOSI/MISO. ADT's enable_cs suggests Apple may drive CS as a GPIO; Linux's controller CS is proven.
pins_and_gpio.spien: AP pin 195 word at 0x23c10030c. Output. Sequence per spi-hid-apple-of.c:22-37: 1, 5 ms, 0, 5 ms, 1, 50 ms.
pins_and_gpio.irq_pin: NUB pin 13 word at 0x23d1f0034. Input. DATA reflects the pin level in input modes (apple_gpio_get, :214-226), so first bring-up can poll the level (active low) with no AIC/GPIO interrupt plumbing.
pins_and_gpio.recommendation: Read back every pin word before and after the change, including LOCK and GRP. If LOCK is set, stop; never force it.

spi_controller_pio.clock: 120 MHz input. CLKDIV = ceil(120e6/8e6) = 15 gives exactly 8 MHz. Assuming the 24 MHz refclk would give divider 3, i.e. a 40 MHz bus.
spi_controller_pio.format: Mode 0 (no CPHA/CPOL in Linux DT), MSB first, 8-bit words. FIFO depth 16. PIO only; do not use the SIO DMA channels in the ADT (they need the SIO coprocessor).
spi_controller_pio.sequence: spi-apple.c init :161-187 then transfer :460-566. Reset FIFOs, clear IF_XFER/IF_FIFO, set TXCNT/RXCNT, prime TX, RUN, then service the FIFOs until the TXCOMPLETE/RXCOMPLETE flags are set, with a 200 ms budget, drain RX, then CTRL=0.
spi_controller_pio.chip_select: Software CS through APPLE_SPI_PIN bit1, active low: assert, 65 us, transfers, 65 us, deassert, then at least 250 us before the next assert. The aurora hardware-CS-delay path is Mesa-only (:610-618) and must not be used for the keyboard.
spi_controller_pio.messages: Write = one CS window: 256-byte TX, 200 us gap (SPI_RW_CHG_DELAY_US), 4-byte RX that must read ac 27 68 d5. Read = one CS window with a 256-byte RX.
spi_controller_pio.interrupt: AIC 617 (controller) is optional: polling is fine at 8 MHz for 256 bytes. Under the HV, guest MMIO to SPI3, GPIO and nub-gpio is not trapped by the current m1n1 configuration.

protocol_for_grok.packet: 256 bytes, little-endian: flags u8 (0x40 write/response, 0x20 device read), device u8 (0xd0 info, 0 mgmt, 1 kbd, 2 tp, 3 aux), offset le16, remain le16, length le16, data[246], crc16 le16 over bytes 0..253 (core.c:195-204).
protocol_for_grok.crc: Linux crc16(0, ...) is CRC-16/ARC: reflected poly 0x8005 (0xA001), init 0, no final xor. Use it for both the packet CRC and the message CRC. It is not CCITT.
protocol_for_grok.message: Header {u0, u1, u2, id, rsplen le16, length le16} (8 bytes), payload, then message crc16 over header+payload. Packet length = 8 + payload + 2.
protocol_for_grok.boot: After spien, while the IRQ pin is low, read a packet with length 4 and data a0 80 00 00 (packet CRC must be valid). Wait up to 1 s.
protocol_for_grok.requests: device info (target 0xd0: 0x20,0x01,0xd0, rsplen 0); interface info i=0..n-1 (0x20,0x02,i, rsplen 512); HID descriptor i=1..n-1 (0x20,0x10,i, rsplen 512). Responses come back with flags 0x40 and the same u0/u1; u2 selects device/interface.
protocol_for_grok.input: flags 0x20, device 1, u0 0x10, payload = HID input report. Device 0 with u1 0xe0 is a 5-byte status report.
protocol_for_grok.reassembly: offset==0 and remain==0 is a single packet. Otherwise concatenate while offset equals bytes so far, and total = offset + length + remain stays constant.

do_not_port.defect: GET_REPORT copies max(len, reply_len) into a len-byte caller buffer. Use min.
The device-info serial string is copied into the vendor buffer. Copy into serial, and redact it in logs and receipts.
Reassembly bounds the total by U16_MAX, but the buffer is 0x800 (:1073), so a CRC-valid malformed sequence overflows. Bound total <= buffer size, and length <= 246.

RX reads the whole FIFO level even when it exceeds the words remaining (only WARN_ON), overflowing the 4-byte status buffer (:1066) on stale FIFO data. Clamp reads to the words remaining, or discard the excess.
A status mismatch only warns and the write is still reported as success. A diagnostic should record it as a failed write, not a success.

console_path.existing_bridge: IOHIDEventService.cpp:1794-1795 calls PDHIDPushKeyboardEvent for keyboard-page usages <= 0xE7. PDHIDEventQueue.cpp:536-560 queues the usage, and :475-477 feeds the bytes to cons_cinput. The same path serves IOUSBHIDKeyboard and ApplePS2Keyboard.
console_path.implication: A native SPI-HID IOHIDDevice that publishes the device's real descriptor and reports must get an IOHIDEventService/IOHIDEventDriver match before typing reaches the shell. Proving the transport (logged raw reports) and proving shell typing are separate milestones.

recommended_diagnostic_stages: S0 read-only: SPI3/SPI_P/SIO/GPIO/NUB_GPIO PS words; AP 46-49 and 195 and NUB 13 pin words. No SPI3 MMIO if SPI3 ACTUAL != 0xf.
S1 power and pinmux with read-back; stop on LOCK or on a timeout reaching 0xf.
S2 spien sequence; poll NUB 13 low; read and verify the boot packet.
S3 device info, with the serial string redacted; S4 interface info and descriptors, logging lengths and CRC results.
S5 log raw keyboard input reports for a bounded window. No console injection, no success stubs, no retry loops beyond the per-transfer budgets.
S6 IOHIDDevice publication and the event path; only then claim typing.

inventory_tool_review.verdict: APPROVE. Read-only registry matching, names and class names only; no service open, no HID queue. Uses the tiny PDIOKitLib surface consistently (char* IOServiceMatching, 3-argument IOServiceGetMatchingServices, IOObjectGetClass). Absent classes produce an empty iterator, not an error, so the expected-absent PDM1SPIHID/AppleEmbeddedKeyboard do not set query_errors.
inventory_tool_review.correction_2026_11_07: The earlier verdict's last sentence was wrong. In XNU, is_io_service_get_matching_services returns kIOReturnSuccess with a NULL iterator for no matches (copyExistingServices returns NULL and IOUserIterator::withIterator(NULL) returns NULL; IOUserClient.cpp:437-443, 2767-2768), so the original code's 'else failed = 1' set query_errors for the absent AppleEmbeddedKeyboard/PDM1SPIHID classes. Root's fix (keyboard_inventory.c 48cad701, original preserved as inventory/attempts/005 2a57ecfc) changes it to 'else if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS) failed = 1'. Reviewed: correct and minimal. Inventory output is diagnostic only, never input proof.

not_established: Runtime register values at handoff (power states, pin words, LOCK/GRP) on this machine.
Whether group 0 or group 6 is the right interrupt group for NUB 13 under Darwin; polling avoids depending on either.
